figurative_meaning_en: A person who expects favors or mercy from others
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে তীর্থের কাকের মতো সর্বদা অন্যের কাছে দান-খয়রাত আশা করে।
এই লোকটি তীর্থের কাক, কখনো নিজে কিছু করে না, শুধু অনুগ্রহ চায়।
example_sentences_in_english: He is like the crow of the pilgrimage site, always expecting alms from others.
That man is a tirtha crow, never doing anything himself but seeking favors everywhere.
history: The idiom draws from the common sight of crows scavenging for food offerings at Hindu pilgrimage sites (tirthas), symbolizing opportunistic beggars who rely on devotees' charity.
note: The idiom reflects Hindu cultural practices of almsgiving at sacred sites.
